trace.rewrite: Contract Act section 23 unlawful consideration void agreement
trace.hyde: Where the consideration or object of an agreement is unlawful, such agreement shall be deemed void ab initio. It is a settled principle of law that no contract can be enforced if the underlying consideration is forbidden by law, is of such a nature that it would defeat the provisions of any law, or is regarded by the court as immoral or opposed to public policy. Consequently, any agreement entered into with an unlawful consideration lacks the essential legal sanctity required for enforceability, rendering the entire transaction null and void in the eyes of the law, and no relief can be granted by this court in respect thereof.

trace.rewrite: gratuitous bailment reimbursement of expenses Contract Act section 158
trace.hyde: Where a person undertakes to store or transport goods for another party without the receipt of any remuneration or consideration, such gratuitous bailee shall nonetheless be entitled to be indemnified by the bailor for all necessary and reasonable expenses incurred in the course of the bailment. The law mandates that the bailor shall repay to the bailee all such costs as were essential for the preservation and safe carriage of the goods, notwithstanding the absence of a fee. Any expenditure incurred by the bailee in the discharge of their duties, which was not otherwise contemplated by the parties, shall be recoverable as a debt due from the bailor.

trace.rewrite: gratuitous bailment revocation before expiry of term liability for loss Contract Act
trace.hyde: Where a thing is lent gratuitously for a specific duration, the lender may, notwithstanding the term stipulated, demand the restitution of the chattel at any time should an urgent necessity arise. However, if the borrower has incurred expenses or suffered loss by reason of such premature termination, the lender shall be liable to indemnify the borrower for all such losses as were reasonably foreseeable at the time of the contract. The court shall, in determining the quantum of damages, have regard to the nature of the item and the extent of the prejudice caused to the borrower by the sudden deprivation of use.

trace.rewrite: lessee liability for damage to property due to unauthorized use under Contract Act
trace.hyde: Where a lessee utilizes the demised property in a manner inconsistent with the express terms of the lease agreement, thereby occasioning damage to the subject matter, such lessee shall be held strictly liable for the resultant loss. It is a settled principle of law that any deviation from the stipulated purpose of use constitutes a breach of covenant, rendering the lessee obligated to indemnify the lessor for the diminution in value or the cost of restoration. Consequently, the lessee is legally bound to compensate the lessor for all damages sustained as a direct consequence of such unauthorized usage, notwithstanding any prior possession or contractual arrangement.

trace.rewrite: Contract Act Section 74 liquidated damages court power to award compensation exceeding stipulated amount
trace.hyde: Where a contract specifies a sum to be paid in case of a breach, the court shall not award by way of compensation any sum exceeding the amount so named. The party complaining of the breach is entitled to receive from the party who has broken the contract reasonable compensation not exceeding the amount so named, whether or not actual damage or loss is proved to have been caused thereby. The court is precluded from granting damages in excess of the liquidated sum stipulated by the parties, as the intention of the legislature is to restrict recovery to the agreed threshold, ensuring certainty in contractual obligations and preventing punitive assessments.

trace.rewrite: Contract Act 1872 section 53 prevention of performance by promisee liability
trace.hyde: Where a party to a contract, by their own omission or failure to provide the requisite access, information, or cooperation, prevents the other party from performing their obligations, such non-performance shall not be actionable against the performing party. It is a settled principle of law that no person may derive a benefit from their own default or negligence. Consequently, where the promisee hinders the promisor in the execution of the agreed service, the promisor is discharged from liability for any resulting delay or failure to complete the work, and the promisee shall be estopped from claiming damages for such non-performance under the provisions of the Contract Act.

trace.rewrite: appropriation of payments by creditor where debtor makes no intimation Contract Act section 60
trace.hyde: Where the debtor has omitted to intimate, and there are no other circumstances indicating to which debt the payment is to be applied, the creditor may apply it at his discretion to any lawful debt actually due and payable to him from the debtor, whether its recovery is or is not barred by the law in force for the time being as to the limitation of suits. Provided that such application shall not be made to a debt which is disputed by the debtor, and the creditor shall be bound to provide a clear accounting of such appropriation upon the demand of the debtor.

trace.rewrite: Contract Act Section 49 place of performance where no place is fixed
trace.hyde: Where a contract is silent regarding the place of performance and no specific request is made by the promisee in this behalf, it shall be the duty of the promisor to apply to the promisee to appoint a reasonable place for the performance of the promise, and to perform the contract at such place as is appointed. In the absence of such appointment or application, the promisor must exercise due diligence to perform the obligation at a location that is reasonable under the circumstances, ensuring that the intent of the parties is upheld in accordance with the principles of equity and the prevailing law of contract.

trace.rewrite: Contract Act 1872 Section 126 contract of guarantee oral or written
trace.hyde: In the interpretation of Section 126 of the Contract Act, 1872, it is observed that the statute defines a contract of guarantee as a contract to perform the promise, or discharge the liability, of a third person in case of his default. Upon a plain reading of the provision, it is manifest that the legislature has not prescribed any mandatory requirement for such a contract to be reduced into writing. Consequently, it is settled legal position that a contract of guarantee may be either oral or written, provided that the essential elements of a valid contract, including offer, acceptance, and consideration, are duly established by the parties involved.

trace.rewrite: co-sureties liability contribution Contract Act section 146
trace.hyde: Where two or more persons are co-sureties for the same debt or duty, whether made jointly or severally, and whether under the same or different contracts, and whether with or without the knowledge of each other, the principal debtor having made default, such co-sureties shall, in the absence of any contract to the contrary, be liable to contribute equally to the discharge of the whole debt or such part thereof as remains unpaid by the principal debtor. Any co-surety who has paid more than their proportionate share of the debt shall be entitled to recover the excess from the other co-sureties, in accordance with the principles of equity and contribution.

trace.rewrite: punishment for rash driving on a public way under Pakistan Penal Code
trace.hyde: Whoever drives any vehicle, or rides, on any public way in a manner so rash or negligent as to endanger human life, or to be likely to cause hurt or injury to any other person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to three thousand rupees, or with both. The court, while determining the quantum of sentence, shall take into account the gravity of the endangerment caused to the public and the potential for grievous harm resulting from such reckless conduct upon the thoroughfare.

trace.rewrite: Pakistan Penal Code section 357 punishment for assault in attempt to wrongfully confine
trace.hyde: Whoever assaults or uses criminal force to any person, in attempting wrongfully to confine that person, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to three thousand rupees, or with both. The legislative intent behind this provision is to safeguard the liberty of the individual against unlawful restraint, ensuring that any attempt to deprive a citizen of their freedom through force or assault is met with strict penal consequences under the Pakistan Penal Code, thereby upholding the fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution.

trace.rewrite: legal consequences of advocating against sovereignty of Pakistan Penal Code sedition
trace.hyde: Whoever by words, either spoken or written, or by signs, or by visible representation, or otherwise, brings or attempts to bring into hatred or contempt, or excites or attempts to excite disaffection towards the Federal Government established by law, or advocates the cessation of the sovereignty of Pakistan, shall be punished with imprisonment for life or with imprisonment which may extend to ten years, to which fine may be added. Any person found guilty of such seditious acts, which threaten the territorial integrity and the constitutional foundation of the State, shall be liable to prosecution under the relevant penal provisions governing high treason and the maintenance of public order.

trace.rewrite: PPC Section 419 cheating by personation non-existent person
trace.hyde: The essential ingredients of the offence of cheating by personation require the accused to pretend to be some other person, whether real or fictitious. It is the settled position of law that the identity assumed need not belong to a living or existing individual. The gravamen of the offence lies in the fraudulent or dishonest representation made by the accused to induce the delivery of property or the commission of an act. Consequently, the non-existence of the person being impersonated does not absolve the accused of criminal liability, as the deception remains complete upon the successful misrepresentation of a distinct identity to the victim.

trace.rewrite: Section 337Q Pakistan Penal Code 1860 arsh amount for destruction of organ
trace.hyde: Where a person causes the destruction of an organ of another person, the offender shall be liable to pay arsh, which shall be equal to the full diyat. For the purposes of this section, the destruction of an organ refers to the permanent deprivation of the utility of the said organ or the permanent disfigurement thereof. The court, while determining the quantum of arsh, shall ensure that the compensation is commensurate with the gravity of the injury sustained by the victim, in accordance with the principles of Islamic injunctions as prescribed under the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860, ensuring that justice is administered without undue delay or prejudice to the parties involved.

trace.rewrite: punishment for public intoxication and causing annoyance under Pakistan Penal Code
trace.hyde: Whoever, being in a state of intoxication, appears in any public place or in any place which it is a trespass in him to enter, and there conducts himself in such a manner as to cause annoyance to any person, shall be punished with imprisonment for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, or with both. The court, in determining the quantum of sentence, shall have due regard to the gravity of the public nuisance caused and the potential for breach of peace arising from such disorderly conduct within the public domain.

trace.rewrite: punishment for mudihah under Pakistan Penal Code
trace.hyde: Whoever causes to any person a hurt which endangers life or which causes the sufferer to be during the space of twenty days in severe bodily pain, or renders him unable to follow his ordinary pursuits, or disfigures or dismembers any organ of the body, being a hurt designated as mudihah, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to five years, and shall also be liable to fine, provided that such punishment shall be subject to the provisions of Qisas and Diyat as prescribed under the relevant chapters of the Pakistan Penal Code.

trace.rewrite: fraudulent removal or concealment of property to prevent debt recovery Pakistan Penal Code
trace.hyde: Where any person, with the intent to obstruct, delay, or defeat the recovery of a debt or demand, whether due to himself or any other person, fraudulently conceals, removes, or transfers any property or interest therein, such act shall constitute an offence. Notwithstanding any other provision contained herein, any person found guilty of such fraudulent conduct, aimed at preventing the lawful satisfaction of a debt or demand, shall be liable to punishment with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine, or with both, as the court deems fit in the interest of justice.

trace.rewrite: right of private defense causing harm to innocent person Pakistan Penal Code section 96 to 106
trace.hyde: Where an individual, in the exercise of the right of private defense, acts in good faith to avert an imminent threat to their own life, the accidental infliction of harm upon an innocent bystander shall not constitute a criminal offense. Provided that the accused exercised due care and caution, and the harm caused was an unintended consequence of a lawful act performed under the apprehension of death or grievous hurt. The principle of necessity and the right to self-preservation, as recognized under the penal framework, shall protect the accused from criminal liability, provided the force employed was proportionate to the danger faced and not excessive in the circumstances.

trace.rewrite: illegal gratification public servant influence peddling Prevention of Corruption Act
trace.hyde: Whoever accepts, or obtains, or agrees to accept, or attempts to obtain from any person, for himself or for any other person, any gratification whatever, as a motive or reward for inducing, by corrupt or illegal means, any public servant to perform or to forbear from performing any official act, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, or with fine, or with both. The exercise of personal influence for pecuniary gain in the discharge of public functions constitutes a substantive offense against the state, undermining the integrity of the administrative machinery and the sanctity of public office.

trace.rewrite: Article 86 Constitution of Pakistan expenditure authorization after National Assembly dissolution
trace.hyde: Notwithstanding the dissolution of the National Assembly, the Federal Government shall remain empowered to authorize expenditure from the Federal Consolidated Fund to meet the essential requirements of the State. In such circumstances, the executive authority shall ensure that all disbursements are strictly limited to the maintenance of administrative functions and the continuity of public services until such time as a new Assembly is constituted and the budgetary process is resumed in accordance with the constitutional mandate. Any expenditure so authorized shall be placed before the succeeding National Assembly for retrospective approval, ensuring that the principles of fiscal accountability and parliamentary oversight are upheld in the interim period.

trace.rewrite: Article 103 Constitution of Pakistan 1973 disqualification member Provincial Assembly appointment as Governor
trace.hyde: Notwithstanding anything contained in the Constitution, if a member of a Provincial Assembly is appointed as the Governor of a Province, his seat in the Assembly shall become vacant on the day he enters upon his office. The constitutional mandate ensures that no individual shall simultaneously hold the office of a Provincial Governor and retain membership in the Provincial Assembly, thereby upholding the principle of separation of powers and preventing a conflict of interest. Consequently, upon the assumption of the gubernatorial office, the member is deemed to have vacated his legislative seat by operation of law, necessitating a by-election to fill the resultant vacancy in accordance with the prescribed legal procedure.

filters.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973

trace.rewrite: limitation period for appeal by Federation or Province under Article 203F Constitution of Pakistan 1973
trace.hyde: In accordance with the provisions set forth under Article 203F of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973, an appeal against a decision of the Federal Shariat Court may be preferred before the Supreme Court. Where the Federation or a Province is aggrieved by such a judgment, order, or sentence, the period of limitation for filing an appeal shall be sixty days from the date of the impugned decision. This period is strictly construed to ensure the finality of judicial proceedings, provided that the Supreme Court may, in the interest of justice, entertain an appeal after the expiry of the said period if sufficient cause is shown.

filters.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan, 1973

trace.rewrite: judicial review of parliamentary proceedings on grounds of procedural irregularity
trace.hyde: The validity of any proceedings in Parliament shall not be called in question on the ground of any irregularity of procedure. No officer or member of Parliament in whom powers are vested by or under the Constitution for regulating procedure or the conduct of business, or for maintaining order in Parliament, shall be subject to the jurisdiction of any court in respect of the exercise by him of those powers. The internal autonomy of the legislative process remains immune from judicial scrutiny, ensuring that the sanctity of parliamentary deliberations is preserved against challenges predicated upon alleged procedural deviations or technical non-compliance.

trace.rewrite: judicial validation of high treason under Article 6 of the Constitution of Pakistan
trace.hyde: It is hereby declared that the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan constitutes the supreme law of the land, and any act of high treason, as defined under Article 6, constitutes an unpardonable subversion of the constitutional order. No court of law, tribunal, or authority, howsoever constituted, shall possess the jurisdiction or the inherent power to validate, condone, or legitimize any act of high treason. Any purported judicial validation of such an act shall be deemed void ab initio, of no legal effect, and shall not be protected by the doctrine of necessity or any other principle of law, as the Constitution remains inviolable under all circumstances.

filters.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan

trace.rewrite: territorial jurisdiction of Supreme Court of Pakistan judgments and orders
trace.hyde: It is hereby declared and affirmed that the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court of Pakistan, as the apex judicial authority, extends to the whole of Pakistan. Any order, decree, or direction issued by the Court in exercise of its constitutional mandate shall be binding on all executive and judicial authorities throughout the country. The enforcement of such mandates is not restricted to the territorial limits of the Islamabad Capital Territory but shall be executed with full force and effect in every province and territory of the Federation, ensuring the supremacy of law and the uniform administration of justice across the entire sovereign state of Pakistan.

trace.rewrite: Code of Civil Procedure 1908 Section 39 suo motu transfer of decree for execution
trace.hyde: Notwithstanding anything contained in the preceding provisions, the Court may, of its own motion, send a decree for execution to any subordinate Court of competent jurisdiction. The exercise of this power is discretionary and may be invoked by the Court where it deems such transfer necessary for the ends of justice or the effective realization of the decretal amount. Nothing in this section shall be construed as limiting the inherent powers of the Court to ensure that the process of execution is conducted in a manner that is both expeditious and consistent with the procedural requirements stipulated under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.

trace.rewrite: arrest or attachment of property of public officer in official capacity CPC
trace.hyde: No warrant of arrest shall be issued against a public officer in respect of any act purporting to be done by such officer in his official capacity, nor shall any property of such officer be liable to attachment in execution of a decree passed against him in his official capacity, unless the court is satisfied that the act was done with malicious intent or in gross violation of the prescribed procedure. The immunity herein provided is intended to protect the integrity of public functions and shall not be construed to extend to personal liabilities arising from conduct extraneous to the discharge of official duties.

trace.rewrite: CPC Section 47 dispute regarding execution discharge or satisfaction of decree separate suit
trace.hyde: Where any question arises as to the execution, discharge, or satisfaction of a decree, such question shall be determined by the Court executing the decree and not by a separate suit. The legislative intent behind this provision is to ensure the expeditious disposal of matters incidental to the enforcement of judicial orders, thereby preventing the multiplicity of litigation. Consequently, all contentions regarding the validity or fulfillment of the decree must be adjudicated within the scope of the execution proceedings themselves, as the bar against a separate suit is absolute and mandatory in nature, ensuring that the finality of the original judgment remains undisturbed by collateral proceedings.

trace.rewrite: Code of Civil Procedure 1908 Section 86A suit against diplomatic agent
trace.hyde: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Code, no suit shall be instituted against any diplomatic agent of a foreign state, or any person entitled to immunity under the Diplomatic and Consular Privileges Act, without the prior consent of the Federal Government, certified in writing by a Secretary to the Government of Pakistan. Any proceedings initiated in contravention of this provision shall be deemed void ab initio, as the immunity granted to such representatives under international law and domestic statutes serves as an absolute bar to the jurisdiction of any civil court, unless such consent is expressly obtained and produced before the court at the time of the institution of the suit.

trace.rewrite: High Court execution of decree before taxation of costs CPC
trace.hyde: It is hereby clarified that the pendency of the taxation of costs shall not operate as a bar to the execution of a decree passed by this Court. The decree-holder is entitled to seek enforcement of the substantive relief granted, notwithstanding that the precise quantum of costs remains to be ascertained by the taxing officer. The procedural requirement of calculating costs is ancillary to the main decree and does not constitute a condition precedent for the issuance of execution proceedings. Consequently, the High Court maintains the inherent jurisdiction to order the execution of a decree, ensuring that the fruits of litigation are not unduly delayed by the administrative finalization of costs.

trace.rewrite: Court Fees Act deficiency in court fee payment at time of filing and subsequent extension
trace.hyde: Where the plaint or any other document is filed without the payment of the requisite court-fee, the Court may, in its discretion, allow the plaintiff or the applicant to supply the requisite stamp-paper or pay the deficiency within a period fixed by the Court. Upon such payment within the stipulated time, the document shall have the same force and effect as if it had been originally filed with the proper court-fee. The Court, for sufficient cause shown, may extend the period for such payment, provided that the failure to pay was not due to contumacy or gross negligence on the part of the party concerned.

trace.rewrite: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 Section 72 income from discontinued business
trace.hyde: Where any business, profession, or vocation has been permanently discontinued, any sum received after the cessation of such activity, which would have been chargeable to tax as income had it been received prior to the discontinuance, shall be deemed to be the income of the person receiving such sum in the tax year of receipt. Notwithstanding the cessation of the underlying source, the provisions of this Ordinance shall apply to such receipts as if the business or source were still in existence, thereby ensuring that all accrued economic gains remain subject to the levy of income tax in accordance with the prescribed rates and legal requirements.

trace.rewrite: definition of associates under Income Tax Ordinance 2001 common employment
trace.hyde: It is hereby clarified that the mere existence of a common employer does not, by operation of law, establish a nexus of association between two individuals. For the purposes of determining liability or conflict of interest, the term associate shall not be construed to encompass persons whose only connection is the shared status of employment within the same corporate entity. Absent evidence of a concerted effort, shared financial interest, or a relationship beyond the professional scope of their duties, the court finds that common employment is insufficient to satisfy the threshold of association required under the relevant provisions of the Act.

trace.rewrite: Section 100B Income Tax Ordinance 2001 capital gain tax computation mutual funds insurance companies
trace.hyde: Notwithstanding the general provisions governing the taxation of capital gains under this Ordinance, the computation of tax liability for mutual funds and insurance companies shall be governed by the specific modalities prescribed under Section 100B. It is hereby clarified that the legislature has carved out a distinct fiscal regime for these entities, thereby excluding them from the uniform application of capital gain tax computation rules applicable to other corporate bodies. Consequently, the tax treatment of capital gains arising from the disposal of securities by such entities must strictly adhere to the specialized mechanism stipulated in the Second Schedule, ensuring that the unique regulatory framework governing these financial institutions remains undisturbed by general taxation principles.

trace.rewrite: Income Tax Ordinance tax treatment of lump sum royalty payment for literary work exceeding 24 months
trace.hyde: Where the time taken by the author of a literary or artistic work in the making thereof exceeds twenty-four months, the assessee may, upon application to the Commissioner, elect to spread the receipt of any lump sum royalty payment over the period of such work. The tax liability shall be computed by apportioning the income equally across the relevant financial years, provided that the total duration of the engagement is duly substantiated by evidence. This provision ensures that the tax burden is mitigated in accordance with the principles of equitable assessment, notwithstanding the provisions contained in the Income Tax Ordinance regarding the year of receipt.

trace.rewrite: legal obligation to report terrorism suspicion during employment Pakistan
trace.hyde: Every person, including any employee or official acting in the course of their professional duties, who possesses information or entertains a reasonable suspicion regarding the commission of an act of terrorism or the presence of a proscribed individual, shall be under a mandatory legal obligation to report such information to the nearest police station or law enforcement agency without delay. Failure to disclose such material facts, where there exists a credible basis for suspicion, shall render the individual liable to prosecution under the relevant provisions of the Anti-Terrorism Act, as the duty to preserve public order and national security supersedes any claim of professional discretion or personal hesitation.

trace.rewrite: limitation period for appeal against Anti-Terrorism Court conviction
trace.hyde: Any person aggrieved by any final judgment, order or sentence passed by an Anti-terrorism Court may prefer an appeal to the High Court within fifteen days of the passing of such judgment, order or sentence. The period of limitation prescribed herein shall be strictly construed, and no appeal shall be entertained by the High Court after the expiry of the said period, unless the appellant satisfies the Court that there were sufficient grounds for the delay. The appellate jurisdiction shall be exercised in accordance with the provisions of the Anti-terrorism Act, ensuring that the ends of justice are met within the stipulated timeframe provided by the legislature.

trace.rewrite: court power to order witness anonymity voice or face distortion
trace.hyde: In the interest of justice and for the protection of witnesses, the Court is empowered to issue such directions as it deems necessary to ensure the safety and anonymity of a witness. Where the Court is satisfied that the disclosure of the identity of a witness poses a threat to their life or security, it may, in its discretion, order the use of technological measures, including but not limited to, the modulation of voice or the masking of facial features during the course of proceedings. Such measures shall be implemented to preserve the integrity of the trial while safeguarding the witness from potential intimidation or harm.

trace.rewrite: consequence of failure to give notice of talaq to Chairman under section 7 of Muslim Family Laws Ordinance 1961
trace.hyde: Any man who contravenes the provisions of this Ordinance by failing to give the Chairman notice in writing of the pronouncement of talaq in any form whatsoever shall be punishable with simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine which may extend to five thousand rupees, or with both. The failure to notify the Chairman does not render the divorce ineffective under the law, but it constitutes a distinct penal offence for which the husband shall be held liable, notwithstanding the validity of the underlying pronouncement of talaq under the personal law applicable to the parties.

trace.rewrite: procedure for talaq-e-tafweez and dissolution of marriage under Dissolution of Muslim Marriages Act 1939
trace.hyde: Where the right of divorce has been duly delegated to the wife, or where the parties desire to dissolve the marriage otherwise than by talaq, the provisions of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance shall apply mutatis mutandis. The person wishing to effect such dissolution shall, as soon as may be after the pronouncement or execution of the instrument, give the Chairman notice in writing of their intention to do so, and shall supply a copy thereof to the other party. Failure to provide such notice shall constitute an offence punishable under the law, and the dissolution shall not be deemed effective until the expiration of the prescribed period following the receipt of said notice.

trace.rewrite: Muslim Law Laws Ordinance 1961 Arbitration Council Chairman non-Muslim Union Council Chairman procedure
trace.hyde: Where the Chairman of the Union Council is a non-Muslim, he shall not be eligible to act as the Chairman of the Arbitration Council for the purposes of the Muslim Family Laws Ordinance. In such an eventuality, the members of the Union Council shall elect one of their Muslim members to act as the Chairman of the Arbitration Council for the specific matter at hand. The member so elected shall exercise all powers and perform all functions vested in the Chairman of the Union Council under the relevant rules, ensuring that the proceedings remain in accordance with the personal law of the parties concerned.

trace.rewrite: Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010 power of Federal Government to remove difficulties
trace.hyde: If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010, the Federal Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, make such provisions as appear to it to be necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty. Provided that no such order shall be made after the expiry of a period of two years from the commencement of this Act. Every order made under this section shall, as soon as may be after it is made, be laid before each House of Majlis-e-Shoora (Parliament) for consideration and approval.

trace.rewrite: Anti-Money Laundering Act 2010 search and seizure without warrant procedure
trace.hyde: Where an investigating officer has reasonable grounds to believe that any evidence, record, or property related to an offence of money laundering is likely to be concealed, destroyed, or tampered with, and the delay occasioned by obtaining a warrant would defeat the purpose of the investigation, the officer may, after recording the reasons in writing, proceed to search and seize such material forthwith. The officer shall, within forty-eight hours of such action, submit a detailed report to the Special Court, justifying the exigency of the circumstances and the necessity of the immediate search, whereupon the Court shall review the legality of the action taken and pass such orders as it deems fit.

trace.rewrite: public disclosure of assets of civil servants BS-17 and above Pakistan
trace.hyde: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the declaration of assets and liabilities submitted by civil servants in BS-17 and above shall be treated as confidential documents. Such declarations shall not be subject to public disclosure or inspection under the Right of Access to Information Act, 2017, unless specifically authorized by the competent authority in the interest of public accountability. The preservation of these records remains the exclusive domain of the designated administrative department, and no citizen shall be entitled to seek copies thereof as a matter of right, ensuring the protection of privacy and the integrity of the civil service structure.

trace.rewrite: termination of civil servant due to abolition of post or reduction in cadre strength seniority rules
trace.hyde: Where a post in a civil service or a cadre is abolished or the number of posts is reduced, the principle of seniority shall be strictly observed in determining the order of termination. The civil servant who is junior-most in the relevant cadre or grade shall be the first to be retrenched. Provided that the competent authority shall ensure that such termination is carried out in accordance with the prescribed rules of service, ensuring that no person is removed from service without due consideration of their length of service and the specific requirements of the department, subject to the overriding principles of equity and administrative necessity.

trace.rewrite: Federal Board of Revenue Act 2007 Section 19 power to levy fees and charges
trace.hyde: In exercise of the powers conferred under the Federal Board of Revenue Act, 2007, the Board is empowered to levy and collect such fees and charges as may be prescribed for the provision of services, issuance of certifications, or the facilitation of administrative functions incidental to the discharge of its statutory duties. Such levies shall be determined by the Board to ensure the recovery of costs incurred in the maintenance of electronic systems, data processing, and the enhancement of operational efficiency within the revenue administration framework, provided that all such collections are deposited into the Federal Consolidated Fund in accordance with the established financial procedures of the Government.

trace.rewrite: National Command Authority Act 2010 appellate authority appeal timeframe service terms and conditions
trace.hyde: Any employee aggrieved by an order passed under this Act may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Authority within thirty days of the communication of such order. The Appellate Authority shall, upon receipt of the appeal, consider the merits of the case and dispose of the matter within a period of ninety days. The decision rendered by the Appellate Authority in this regard shall be final and binding upon the parties, and no further representation or petition shall be entertained against the said determination, save as provided under the relevant service rules applicable to the employees of the National Command Authority.

trace.rewrite: Provincial Government argument electricity duty private entities generators 500 KW 2001 Ordinance
trace.hyde: The learned counsel for the Provincial Government contended that the Electricity Duty Ordinance, 2001, operates as a comprehensive fiscal measure intended to capture all forms of self-generated power. It was argued that the legislative intent behind the Ordinance was to impose liability upon all private entities operating power generation sets exceeding 500 KW, irrespective of whether such electricity is consumed for industrial or commercial purposes. The State maintained that the exemption clauses must be construed narrowly, and that the mere act of generation by private entities constitutes a taxable event under the statute, thereby mandating the payment of electricity duty to the provincial exchequer without exception.

trace.rewrite: Supreme Court judgment Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Medical Teaching Institutions doctors promotion
trace.hyde: In the matter concerning the promotion of doctors within the Medical Teaching Institutes of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, the Supreme Court of Pakistan has unequivocally held that the principles of natural justice and the statutory framework governing service structures must be strictly adhered to. The Court observed that promotions cannot be treated as a matter of unfettered discretion but must be based on transparent criteria, seniority, and merit as prescribed under the relevant regulations. Consequently, the Court directed the provincial authorities to ensure that all pending promotion cases are finalized in accordance with the established legal mandate, ensuring that no eligible medical professional is deprived of their legitimate right to career progression.

trace.rewrite: Section 302(b) PPC conviction sentence and compensation terms 15 October 2005 incident
trace.hyde: The learned Trial Court, upon careful consideration of the evidence brought on record regarding the incident dated 15 October 2005, found the accused guilty of the offence punishable under Section 302(b) of the Pakistan Penal Code. Consequently, the court sentenced the convict to death as Tazir. Furthermore, in accordance with the provisions of Section 544-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the court directed the convict to pay a sum of rupees one hundred thousand as compensation to the legal heirs of the deceased. In default of such payment, the convict shall undergo further imprisonment for a period of six months.

trace.rewrite: raising new plea regarding nature of property ownership for the first time in Supreme Court
trace.hyde: It is a settled principle of law that a party cannot be permitted to agitate a fresh plea or raise a new contention regarding the nature of property ownership for the first time before the Supreme Court, particularly when such a plea was neither raised in the original pleadings nor canvassed before the trial court or the High Court. The jurisdiction of this Court is essentially appellate in nature, and allowing a party to introduce a novel case at this terminal stage would not only prejudice the opposing party but also violate the fundamental rules of procedure governing the finality of litigation and the scope of judicial review.

trace.rewrite: Supreme Court of Pakistan judgment on locus standi of non-appealing party to challenge dismissal of leave petition filed by another party
trace.hyde: It is a settled principle of law that a party who has failed to challenge the judgment of the High Court by way of an independent petition for leave to appeal cannot subsequently agitate grievances regarding the dismissal of a petition filed by a co-party. The Supreme Court has consistently held that a non-appealing party lacks the locus standi to claim entitlement to notice or relief in proceedings where they have acquiesced to the impugned order. Consequently, such a party cannot seek to revive a settled controversy or complain of procedural prejudice when they themselves neglected to invoke the appellate jurisdiction of this Court within the prescribed period of limitation.

trace.rewrite: embezzlement case restitution of public funds and medical grounds for sentence mitigation Supreme Court of Pakistan
trace.hyde: In the matter of misappropriation of public funds, where the petitioner has already deposited the entire embezzled amount into the national exchequer, the learned counsel for the petitioner submitted that the petitioner is a first-time offender and the sole breadwinner for his family. It was further highlighted that the petitioner's wife is suffering from chronic renal failure, requiring urgent and expensive medical treatment. Consequently, the counsel prayed that in view of the restitution of the public money and the humanitarian grounds concerning the health of the petitioner's spouse, the sentence of imprisonment and the fine imposed by the trial court may be set aside or reduced to the period already undergone.

trace.rewrite: legal obligation of police after dismissal of pre-arrest bail application
trace.hyde: Upon the dismissal of a petition for pre-arrest bail by a court of competent jurisdiction, the protective umbrella of interim relief stands immediately vacated. Consequently, the police authorities are not only empowered but legally obligated to execute the arrest of the accused without further delay. The dismissal of such application removes any procedural bar to detention, and the investigating officer is duty-bound to ensure the accused is taken into custody in accordance with the provisions of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, to facilitate the ongoing investigation and ensure the due process of law is maintained without obstruction or undue interference.

trace.rewrite: Order V Rule 20 CPC requirements for substituted service
trace.hyde: Before the Court may direct service of summons by substituted mode under Order V, Rule 20 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, it must be satisfied upon an application supported by affidavit that there is reason to believe that the defendant is keeping out of the way for the purpose of avoiding service, or that for any other reason the summons cannot be served in the ordinary way. The Court shall record its satisfaction regarding the futility of conventional service before ordering service by affixation or publication, ensuring that the defendant is afforded a reasonable opportunity to be apprised of the proceedings initiated against them.

trace.rewrite: Supreme Court of Pakistan judgment property transfer attorney sons cheque payment without agreement to sell validity
trace.hyde: The Supreme Court has consistently held that a mere issuance of a cheque, in the absence of a formal agreement to sell or cogent evidence of a concluded contract, is insufficient to establish a valid transfer of title. Where an attorney-at-law facilitates the transfer of property to his own sons under such dubious circumstances, the transaction is rendered voidable. The fiduciary relationship imposes a heightened burden of proof upon the attorney to demonstrate the bona fide nature of the consideration. Absent such proof, the court shall not countenance the alienation of property, as the lack of a written instrument and the conflict of interest vitiate the entire transaction.

trace.rewrite: Income Tax Ordinance 2001 failure to collect advance tax on prepaid cards by telecommunications company
trace.hyde: Where a telecommunications company, being a service provider, fails to collect advance tax from its franchisees at the time of issuance or sale of prepaid cards, such company shall be held personally liable for the payment of the tax amount not so collected. The failure to deduct or collect tax as mandated under the provisions of the 2001 Ordinance shall render the licensee subject to recovery proceedings, including the imposition of default surcharge and penalties as prescribed by law. The liability of the company remains primary and absolute, notwithstanding any contractual arrangements with the franchisees, and the Commissioner may initiate recovery of such outstanding tax dues as arrears of land revenue.

trace.rewrite: Supreme Court of Pakistan Trading Corporation of Pakistan performance guarantee refund judgment
trace.hyde: The Supreme Court of Pakistan, while adjudicating the dispute between the Trading Corporation of Pakistan and the respondent, held that the encashment of a performance guarantee is an independent contract, distinct from the underlying commercial agreement. The Court observed that unless there is a clear case of fraud or irretrievable injustice, the bank is obligated to honor the guarantee upon demand. Consequently, the Court ruled that the respondent was not entitled to a refund of the performance guarantee, as the appellant had acted within the terms of the instrument, and the judicial intervention in such banking transactions must remain strictly limited to prevent commercial instability.

trace.rewrite: father suit for maintenance against daughter Supreme Court observation on withdrawal
trace.hyde: In the matter of maintenance recovery, the Honorable Supreme Court has observed that a suit filed by a father against his daughter, predicated solely upon her gainful employment, is fundamentally misconceived and contrary to the moral and legal obligations inherent in the parent-child relationship. The Court has emphasized that such litigation, being vexatious in nature, ought to be withdrawn by the petitioner. It is held that the daughter’s financial independence does not absolve the father of his duty to maintain familial harmony, and the pursuit of recovery against one’s own progeny in such circumstances is viewed as an abuse of the process of law, warranting immediate cessation of proceedings.

trace.rewrite: wife infertility effect on dower and maintenance entitlement Supreme Court of Pakistan
trace.hyde: The legal obligation of a husband to provide maintenance and the wife's entitlement to dower are absolute rights arising from the contract of marriage under Islamic law as interpreted by the Supreme Court of Pakistan. Infertility, whether pre-existing or subsequent to the marriage, does not constitute a valid legal ground for the husband to withhold maintenance or evade the payment of dower. The marital bond remains intact notwithstanding the inability to procreate, and the husband's duty to support his wife persists as a primary liability. Any attempt to link the discharge of these financial obligations to the biological capacity of the wife is repugnant to the principles of justice and the injunctions of Islam.

trace.rewrite: Supreme Court judgment on High Court power to decree suit in family law writ jurisdiction
trace.hyde: The High Court, in exercise of its revisional jurisdiction, erred by setting aside the concurrent findings of the Family Court and the Appellate Court and proceeding to decree the suit of the wife in its entirety. Upon review, the Supreme Court held that the High Court exceeded its limited jurisdiction under the relevant family laws. It was observed that the High Court is not empowered to act as a trial court or to substitute its own findings of fact for those of the courts below. Consequently, the order of the High Court decreeing the suit was set aside, and the matter was remanded for a fresh determination in accordance with the law.

trace.rewrite: Constitution of Pakistan reserved seats for women and non-Muslims allocation controversy Supreme Court judgment
trace.hyde: The primary legal controversy pertains to the interpretation of Article 51 and Article 106 of the Constitution, specifically concerning the proportional representation of reserved seats. The core dispute arises where a political party fails to submit a list of candidates for reserved seats prior to the general election, thereby raising the question of whether such seats can be subsequently allocated to other parties. The judiciary must determine if the constitutional mandate for proportional representation is absolute or contingent upon the timely submission of party lists, balancing the principles of democratic representation against the strict procedural requirements prescribed under the Elections Act, 2017, and the constitutional framework governing the composition of the Assemblies.

filters.act: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan

trace.rewrite: Supreme Court of Pakistan judgment Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Service Tribunal employment status relief
trace.hyde: Upon consideration of the petitions challenging the impugned judgments of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Service Tribunal, this Court finds that the petitioners were entitled to the regularization of their services in accordance with the prevailing policy. Consequently, the petitions are allowed, and the impugned judgments are set aside. The respondents are directed to regularize the services of the petitioners from the date of their initial appointment, with all consequential benefits, including seniority and back benefits, to be calculated and released within a period of sixty days from the date of this order. No order as to costs.

trace.rewrite: Sindh High Court judgment November 7 2024 lawyers filing FIRs against clients observations
trace.hyde: The Court observes with profound concern the emerging and reprehensible trend wherein legal practitioners, in a blatant abuse of professional privilege, are increasingly resorting to the registration of criminal cases against their own clients. Such conduct not only undermines the sanctity of the attorney-client relationship but also constitutes a gross violation of professional ethics. The Court unequivocally deprecates this practice, noting that the initiation of FIRs by counsel against those they are mandated to represent is antithetical to the administration of justice. Consequently, the Court directs that such actions shall be viewed as professional misconduct, warranting stringent disciplinary proceedings to preserve the integrity of the legal profession.

trace.rewrite: procedural history medical board application medico-legal certificate FIR 379/2026
trace.hyde: In the matter of FIR No. 379/2026, the petitioner initially moved an application before the learned Trial Court seeking the constitution of a medical board to re-examine the Medico-Legal Certificates. The said application was dismissed by the Trial Court on the grounds of being premature. Aggrieved by the order, the petitioner preferred a criminal revision before the High Court. Upon hearing the parties, this Court observed that the veracity of the medical evidence is a matter of trial. Consequently, the revision petition was disposed of with the direction that the petitioner may raise these objections during the cross-examination of the medical officer, preserving the right to seek expert opinion under the relevant provisions of the Qanun-e-Shahadat Order.

trace.rewrite: Lahore High Court uniform rate per marla compensation Land Acquisition Act Regular First Appeal
trace.hyde: In the matter of the Regular First Appeal concerning the acquisition of land, the Lahore High Court, upon careful consideration of the evidence and the prevailing market trends, determined that the compensation for the acquired land shall be fixed at a uniform rate of rupees fifty thousand per marla. This determination was predicated on the principle of just compensation, ensuring that the landowners are not deprived of the fair market value of their property. The Court observed that such uniformity is essential to prevent discriminatory treatment and to maintain equity, thereby aligning the compensation with the potential utility and the geographical significance of the subject land at the time of notification.

trace.rewrite: Lahore High Court procedure non-joinder of necessary parties withdrawal of suit
trace.hyde: Where it is manifest that the suit suffers from the non-joinder of necessary parties, and both the plaintiff and the defendant are in consensus regarding the withdrawal of the proceedings, the Court may, in the interest of justice and to prevent a multiplicity of litigation, permit the withdrawal of the suit with liberty to institute a fresh suit in respect of the same subject matter. Such procedural course ensures that the rights of all interested parties are duly adjudicated upon, thereby upholding the principles of equity and preventing the passing of an ineffective decree in the absence of those whose presence is essential for a complete and final determination of the controversy.

trace.rewrite: Section 552 CrPC child marriage girl under 16 years Supreme Court Lahore High Court judgment
trace.hyde: In the matter of a minor female below the age of sixteen years produced before the Court under Section 552 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, it is held that the purported marriage is void ab initio. The Court observed that the statutory prohibition against child marriage overrides any claim of free will or consent by a minor. Consequently, the custody of the minor is restored to her lawful guardians, and the alleged husband is restrained from exercising any marital rights. The Court further directed the local authorities to ensure the protection of the minor, emphasizing that the welfare of the child remains the paramount consideration in all such judicial determinations.

trace.rewrite: Lahore High Court judgment LLB examination passing in parts and first attempt failure
trace.hyde: The Lahore High Court has consistently held that the policy of allowing candidates to pass the LL.B. examinations in parts, or permitting the accumulation of credits across multiple attempts, is subject to the strict regulatory framework prescribed by the University and the Pakistan Bar Council. The Court has observed that the privilege of clearing subjects in installments cannot be construed as an absolute right to circumvent the mandatory requirement of passing the entire examination within the stipulated attempts. Consequently, any failure to qualify within the prescribed first attempt or subsequent permissible chances renders the candidate ineligible for the conferment of the degree, as academic discipline remains paramount to the integrity of the legal profession.

trace.rewrite: appellate court maintenance award wife and minor children family suit
trace.hyde: Upon careful consideration of the evidence and the financial capacity of the appellant, this Court finds that the trial court erred in its assessment of the quantum of maintenance. Consequently, the judgment is modified to reflect the changing economic circumstances of the parties. It is hereby ordered that the appellant shall pay a monthly maintenance allowance of fifteen thousand rupees to the respondent wife and a sum of ten thousand rupees for each of the four minor children, totaling fifty-five thousand rupees per month. This amount shall be payable by the tenth of each calendar month, ensuring the welfare and sustenance of the minors and the wife are adequately secured.

trace.rewrite: registration requirements for private limited company Companies Act 2017
trace.hyde: For the purpose of incorporation of a private limited company, the promoters shall submit to the registrar a memorandum and articles of association, duly signed and witnessed, along with a declaration of compliance with the requirements of the Companies Act, 2017. The application must be accompanied by the prescribed registration fee, the address of the registered office, and particulars of the initial directors. Upon verification of the documents and satisfaction that the proposed company is not formed for any unlawful purpose, the registrar shall issue a certificate of incorporation, which shall serve as conclusive evidence that all requirements of this Act in respect of registration have been complied with.

trace.rewrite: punishment for online bank fraud and phishing under Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act 2016
trace.hyde: Any person who dishonestly gains unauthorized access to a banking system or engages in phishing to obtain sensitive financial data shall be guilty of an offense under the Prevention of Electronic Crimes Act, 2016. Such unauthorized acquisition of data with the intent to cause wrongful loss to a person or wrongful gain to another constitutes a punishable act. Upon conviction, the offender shall be liable to imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine which may extend to one million rupees, or with both, in accordance with the provisions governing electronic fraud and identity theft as stipulated under the said Act.

trace.rewrite: grounds for cancellation of driving license under Motor Vehicles Ordinance 1965
trace.hyde: Under the provisions of the Motor Vehicle Ordinance, 1965, the licensing authority may order the cancellation or suspension of a driving license if the holder is found to be suffering from any disease or physical disability which renders them unfit to drive a motor vehicle. Furthermore, if the holder is convicted of an offense under this Ordinance, or if the authority is satisfied that the holder is a habitual criminal or a danger to the public by reason of their conduct or previous record of driving, the license may be revoked. The authority shall provide the holder an opportunity to be heard before passing such an order of cancellation.

trace.rewrite: minimum number of workers required to form a trade union under Industrial Relations Act 2012
trace.hyde: For the purposes of registration under the Industrial Relations Act, 2012, it is hereby mandated that no trade union of workmen shall be entitled to registration unless it has a minimum membership of at least twenty percent of the total number of workmen employed in the establishment or group of establishments in which it is formed. The Registrar shall satisfy himself that the applicant union fulfills this threshold requirement of membership before issuing a certificate of registration. Any application failing to demonstrate the requisite number of members as prescribed by the statute shall be summarily rejected by the concerned authority in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

trace.rewrite: Election Act 2017 candidate financial disclosure requirements
trace.hyde: Every candidate contesting an election to an assembly shall, along with the nomination papers, submit a statement of assets and liabilities of his own, his spouse and dependents as on the preceding thirtieth day of June. Such statement shall be submitted in the prescribed form and shall be supported by an affidavit. The candidate is mandatorily required to disclose all movable and immovable properties, including investments, bank accounts, and any financial obligations or liabilities, to ensure transparency and accountability in the electoral process as stipulated under the relevant provisions of the Elections Act, 2017, failing which the nomination papers shall be liable to rejection by the Returning Officer.

trace.rewrite: Partnership Act 1932 suit for rendition of accounts by partner against partner
trace.hyde: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, a suit for rendition of accounts by a partner against the firm or any other partner shall be maintainable under the Partnership Act, 1932, provided that the firm is registered and the person suing is or has been shown as a partner in the register of firms. Such a suit shall be instituted in a court of competent jurisdiction, seeking a decree for dissolution of the firm and accounts, or for accounts without dissolution, where the right to such accounts arises from the partnership agreement or the statutory provisions governing the mutual rights and duties of partners.

trace.rewrite: Employees Old-Age Benefits Act 1976 employer obligations and mandatory provisions
trace.hyde: Every employer of an industry or establishment to which this Act applies shall be mandatorily required to register his establishment with the Institution in the prescribed manner. It shall be the statutory duty of such employer to furnish to the Institution, within the stipulated period, all such returns, particulars, and information as may be required for the purposes of this Act. Furthermore, the employer is legally obligated to pay to the Institution, in respect of every person in his insurable employment, contributions at the prescribed rates, and to maintain such records and registers as are necessary to ensure compliance with the provisions of the Employees Old-Age Benefits Act, 1976.

trace.rewrite: Arms Act 1878 penalty for failure to renew license
trace.hyde: Where a license granted under the provisions of the Arms Act, 1878, has expired and the holder thereof fails to apply for its renewal within the prescribed period, such omission shall constitute a contravention of the conditions of the license. Consequently, the person in possession of any arms or ammunition without a valid, subsisting license shall be liable to punishment under the relevant penal provisions of the Act. The court may impose a sentence of imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years, or with a fine, or with both, and the subject arms or ammunition shall be liable to confiscation by the State.

trace.rewrite: Copyright Ordinance 1962 registration procedure for literary work
trace.hyde: Any person desirous of obtaining registration of a literary work under the Copyright Ordinance, 1962, shall make an application in the prescribed form to the Registrar of Copyrights, accompanied by the requisite fee as specified in the Schedule. Upon receipt of such application, the Registrar shall enter the particulars of the work in the Register of Copyrights maintained for this purpose. The registration shall serve as prima facie evidence of the particulars entered therein. Any person aggrieved by an entry made in the Register may apply to the Board for the rectification of such entry in accordance with the procedure prescribed under the rules framed pursuant to this Ordinance.

trace.rewrite: Banking Companies Ordinance 1962 powers to freeze bank account
trace.hyde: Notwithstanding anything contained in any other law for the time being in force, the Banking Company, upon receipt of a directive from the State Bank of Pakistan or a competent court of law, shall be empowered to freeze, suspend, or restrict the operation of any account maintained within its jurisdiction. Such action shall be initiated where there exist reasonable grounds to suspect that the funds are derived from illicit activities, money laundering, or terrorist financing. The Banking Company shall ensure that such freezing is executed with due diligence, and the account holder shall be notified of the grounds for such restriction, subject to the overriding requirements of confidentiality and ongoing investigations.

trace.rewrite: Public Procurement Regulatory Authority (PPRA) Rules 2004 transparency requirements in tender process
trace.hyde: In accordance with the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority Rules, 2004, the procuring agency shall ensure transparency in the tender process by providing equal opportunity to all prospective bidders through wide dissemination of procurement opportunities. The agency is mandated to maintain a fair and objective evaluation process, strictly adhering to the criteria stipulated in the bidding documents. Furthermore, all procurement proceedings shall be conducted in a manner that promotes competition and accountability, ensuring that the results are publicly accessible. Any deviation from these prescribed procedures, which undermines the principles of transparency and open competition, shall render the procurement process liable to challenge under the relevant provisions of the regulatory framework.

trace.rewrite: Pakistan Environmental Protection Act 1997 industrial pollution control standards
trace.hyde: In exercise of the powers conferred under the Pakistan Environmental Protection Act, 1997, the Federal Agency shall establish national environmental quality standards for the discharge of effluents and emissions. No person shall discharge or emit or allow the discharge or emission of any effluent or waste or air pollutant or noise in an amount, concentration or level which is in excess of the National Environmental Quality Standards specified by the Agency. Any industrial activity failing to adhere to these prescribed parameters shall be liable to penalties as stipulated under the Act, ensuring that all industrial operations maintain compliance with the environmental protection framework to mitigate pollution and safeguard public health.

trace.rewrite: Stamp Act 1899 property sale deed stamp duty rates
trace.hyde: In accordance with the provisions of the Stamp Act, 1899, as applicable in the respective provinces, every instrument of conveyance, including a sale deed, shall be chargeable with stamp duty at the rates prescribed in Schedule I of the Act. The quantum of duty is determined based on the value of the consideration set forth in the instrument or the valuation table notified by the Collector, whichever is higher. Parties to the transaction are mandatorily required to ensure that the instrument is duly stamped before registration, failing which the document shall be rendered inadmissible in evidence for any purpose whatsoever under the governing statutory framework.

trace.rewrite: jurisdiction for trademark infringement suit under Trade Marks Ordinance 2001
trace.hyde: In accordance with the provisions of the Trade Marks Ordinance, 2001, any suit for infringement of a registered trade mark or for passing off shall be instituted before the District Court having jurisdiction. No court inferior to that of a District Judge shall have the authority to entertain or adjudicate upon any proceedings arising under this Ordinance. The jurisdiction of the court is determined by the place where the defendant resides, carries on business, or personally works for gain at the time of the commencement of the suit, notwithstanding any other law for the time being in force regarding the territorial competence of civil courts.

trace.rewrite: Contract Act Section 63 remission or extension of time for performance
trace.hyde: Every promisee may dispense with or remit, wholly or in part, the performance of the promise made to him, or may extend the time for such performance, or may accept instead of it any satisfaction which he thinks fit. The failure of a promisor to perform his obligation within the stipulated period shall not render the contract voidable where the promisee has, by his own conduct or express agreement, granted an extension of time or waived his right to demand strict compliance. Such remission or extension shall be legally binding upon the parties, provided that the essential elements of consideration or mutual consent are duly satisfied under the prevailing law.

trace.rewrite: Contract Act Section 68 reimbursement for necessaries supplied to person incapable of contracting
trace.hyde: Where a person, incapable of entering into a contract, or any one whom he is legally bound to support, is supplied by another person with necessaries suited to his condition in life, the person who has furnished such supplies is entitled to be reimbursed from the property of such incapable person. The liability herein created is not founded upon any contract, express or implied, but arises by operation of law to prevent unjust enrichment. Consequently, the claimant may proceed against the estate of the incompetent individual to recover the reasonable value of the goods or services provided, notwithstanding the absence of a valid agreement between the parties.

trace.rewrite: Shamsul Islam Chaudhry Supreme Court of Pakistan judgment principles
trace.hyde: In the matter of Shamsul Islam Chaudhry, the Supreme Court of Pakistan has unequivocally reaffirmed the established principles governing the interpretation of statutory provisions. The Court held that the doctrine of stare decisis remains paramount, ensuring consistency and predictability in judicial pronouncements. It was further observed that any departure from settled law must be grounded in compelling legal necessity and must not undermine the foundational integrity of the judicial system. Consequently, the principles enunciated in the aforementioned judgment continue to serve as binding precedents, mandating strict adherence by all subordinate courts to maintain the sanctity of the rule of law across the jurisdiction.

trace.rewrite: Supreme Court judgment child custody welfare mediation after 14 May 2025 order
trace.hyde: In view of the order dated 14th May 2025, the Court, having regard to the paramount consideration of the welfare of the minor, hereby affirms the settlement reached through the mediation process. It is directed that the custody of the child shall be governed by the terms stipulated in the mediation agreement, which is now incorporated as part of this judgment. The parties are strictly enjoined to adhere to the visitation schedule and welfare provisions contained therein. Any deviation from the agreed terms shall be construed as a violation of this Court’s mandate, and the parties are granted liberty to approach the relevant forum for enforcement of these directions.

trace.rewrite: Lahore High Court judgment suit for declaration and cancellation of mutations Gujrat Additional District Judge 16.02.2019
trace.hyde: Upon careful consideration of the record and the arguments advanced by the learned counsel, this Court finds that the judgment and decree dated 16.02.2019 passed by the learned Additional District Judge, Gujrat, suffers from material irregularities and misappreciation of evidence. Consequently, the revision petition is allowed, and the impugned judgment is set aside. The suit for declaration and cancellation of mutations is hereby dismissed, as the petitioner failed to establish a superior title or prove the alleged fraud. The findings of the trial court are restored, and the mutations in question are declared to be valid and subsisting in accordance with the revenue record.

trace.rewrite: Order XXXIX Rule 1 & 2 CPC interim relief application order dated 16.05.2022
trace.hyde: Upon consideration of the application filed under Order XXXIX Rules 1 and 2 of the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, the learned Trial Court, vide its order dated 16.05.2022, was pleased to dismiss the prayer for interim injunction. The Court observed that the petitioner failed to establish a prima facie case, nor could they demonstrate that the balance of convenience tilted in their favor or that irreparable loss would be occasioned if the relief were declined. Consequently, the application was found devoid of merit and was accordingly rejected, with the parties directed to maintain the status quo until the final adjudication of the main suit.

trace.rewrite: Lahore High Court judgment maintainability of consumer complaint District Consumer Court Bhakkar impugned order 06.10.2026
trace.hyde: Upon consideration of the arguments advanced by the learned counsel, this Court finds that the impugned order dated 06.10.2026 passed by the District Consumer Court, Bhakkar, suffers from a jurisdictional infirmity. It is held that the consumer complaint, in its present form, is not maintainable before the said forum as the cause of action does not fall within the territorial ambit prescribed under the relevant provisions of the Punjab Consumer Protection Act, 2005. Consequently, the proceedings initiated before the District Consumer Court, Bhakkar, are declared coram non judice, and the impugned order is hereby set aside, with liberty granted to the petitioner to approach the court of competent jurisdiction.

trace.rewrite: Lahore High Court judgment FIR 1157/2016 Police Station Shahdara Town
trace.hyde: In the matter of F.I.R. No. 1157 of 2016, registered at Police Station Shahdara Town, the Lahore High Court, upon careful consideration of the material placed on record and the arguments advanced by the learned counsel, has observed that the allegations leveled therein do not constitute a cognizable offence. Consequently, the Court, in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction under Section 561-A of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, has been pleased to quash the said F.I.R. and all subsequent proceedings emanating therefrom, as the continuation of such criminal process would amount to an abuse of the process of the Court and serve no useful purpose.

trace.rewrite: Patents Ordinance 2000 novelty standard for patentability
trace.hyde: For the purposes of this Ordinance, an invention shall be considered new if it does not form part of the state of the art. The state of the art shall be held to comprise everything made available to the public anywhere in the world, by means of a written or oral description, by use, or in any other way, before the date of filing of the application or, if priority is claimed, the priority date of the application. An invention shall be deemed to be new notwithstanding that it may have been disclosed to the public if such disclosure occurred within twelve months preceding the filing date.

trace.rewrite: Civil Aviation Rules 1994 pilot medical fitness standards
trace.hyde: Every flight crew member, including a pilot, shall maintain a standard of medical fitness as prescribed by the Director General in accordance with the international standards set forth by the International Civil Aviation Organization. No person shall exercise the privileges of a license unless they hold a valid medical assessment issued by an authorized medical examiner. The medical fitness requirements shall encompass physical and mental health criteria, including visual, auditory, and cardiovascular standards, to ensure the safe operation of aircraft. Failure to maintain such medical standards shall render the license holder ineligible to perform flight duties, and the Director General may suspend or revoke the license upon finding a breach of these health requirements.

trace.rewrite: Merchant Shipping Ordinance 2001 ship registration procedure
trace.hyde: Every person seeking to register a ship under the Merchant Shipping Ordinance, 2001, shall submit an application in the prescribed form to the Registrar of Ships. The applicant must provide satisfactory evidence of ownership, including the bill of sale or builder's certificate, and ensure the vessel is surveyed for seaworthiness by a recognized surveyor. Upon verification of the particulars and payment of the requisite fees, the Registrar shall enter the ship's details into the Register of Ships and issue a Certificate of Registry. No vessel shall be deemed a Pakistani ship unless it is duly registered in accordance with the provisions of this Ordinance and the rules framed thereunder.

trace.rewrite: Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Act 1976 penalties for unfair means in examination
trace.hyde: Where a candidate is found guilty of using unfair means during an examination conducted under the authority of the Board, the Controller of Examinations or any authorized officer may, after providing a reasonable opportunity of being heard, impose such penalties as deemed appropriate. These penalties may include the cancellation of the current examination paper, disqualification from appearing in subsequent examinations for a specified period, or the forfeiture of results obtained in the relevant academic session. Furthermore, the Board reserves the right to impose a fine or initiate disciplinary proceedings against the candidate, ensuring that the sanctity and integrity of the examination process are strictly maintained in accordance with the provisions of the Act.

filters.act: Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Act, 1976

trace.rewrite: Punjab Healthcare Commission Act 2010 minimum licensing criteria for private hospitals
trace.hyde: No healthcare establishment shall operate within the province of Punjab unless it has been duly registered and licensed by the Punjab Healthcare Commission in accordance with the prescribed standards. Every private hospital is mandatorily required to comply with the minimum service delivery standards, which encompass the availability of qualified medical personnel, adequate diagnostic facilities, adherence to infection control protocols, and the maintenance of patient safety records. Failure to obtain a valid license or to maintain the requisite infrastructure and clinical governance as stipulated under the Act shall render the establishment liable to immediate suspension of services, imposition of financial penalties, or such other punitive measures as the Commission may deem appropriate.

trace.rewrite: Cooperative Societies Act 1925 audit report filing requirements
trace.hyde: Every registered society shall cause its accounts to be audited at least once in every year by an auditor appointed by the Registrar. The submission of the audit report is mandatory to ensure transparency, financial accountability, and the protection of the interests of the members. Failure to submit such report within the prescribed period shall be deemed a contravention of the provisions of the Act, rendering the managing committee liable for penalties. The audit serves as a statutory mechanism to verify that the society’s operations remain in conformity with the objects of its registration and the principles of cooperative management, thereby safeguarding the collective assets of the society against mismanagement or unauthorized diversion of funds.

trace.rewrite: Supreme Court scope of interference in concurrent findings under Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance
trace.hyde: In the matter of concurrent findings rendered by the Rent Controller and the Appellate Court under the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, the Supreme Court has categorically held that the High Court, while exercising revisional jurisdiction, shall not interfere with such findings unless they are shown to be perverse, arbitrary, or based on a misreading of evidence. The High Court is directed to refrain from reappraising the evidence as a court of appeal and must restrict its scrutiny to the legality and propriety of the impugned orders, ensuring that the concurrent conclusions are not disturbed merely on the basis of a different possible view of the facts.
